name: Distributed Vehicle Platooning Benchmark for Hybrid MPC
description: Distributed model predictive control (MPC) is currently being investigated as a solution to the important control challenge presented by networks of hybrid dynamical systems. However, a benchmark problem for distributed hybrid MPC is absent from the literature. We propose distributed control of a platoon of autonomous vehicles as a comparison benchmark problem. The problem provides a complex and adaptable case study, upon which existing and future approaches to distributed MPC for hybrid systems can be evaluated. Two hybrid modeling frameworks are presented for the vehicle dynamics. Five hybrid MPC controllers are then evaluated and extensively assessed on the fleet of vehicles. Finally, we comment on the need for new efficient and high performing distributed MPC schemes for hybrid systems.
evaluation_method: mean tracking error, control cost and rate of constraint violations (safety violations); latency and scalability metrics for distributed controllers
general_score_metric: mean tracking error (with constraint-violation rate and control cost as secondary metrics)
reputation: Recently proposed (2024) as a case study benchmark for distributed hybrid MPC; currently a research prototype rather than a widely adopted community benchmark.
notes: Simulation- and model-dependent benchmark for hybrid dynamical systems; results sensitive to vehicle models, communication delays, and solver implementations; small community adoption to date; not an LLM benchmark.
